verdict.reasoning: Printed page 303 (2014 p.279), 13.8.1: the Term/Subclause table has two aligned rows, '77-level-entry | 13.13, 77-level data description entry' and 'report-group-description-entry | 13.8.4, Report group description entry'. In page-303.md the markdown table holds only the 77-level-entry row; the report-group-description-entry row follows a blank line as a loose paragraph outside the table, with no column separator. Both sources are quoted correctly. The wording is intact, so this is not a normative defect. It is a real structural defect, though, because the table now has one row where the standard prints two, and anything that reads the table as structured data loses the second term-to-subclause mapping. It is not page furniture or line wrapping. Side observation outside this claim: the printed table lists 77-level-entry even though the 13.8.1 format uses constant-entry, not 77-level-entry; the markdown copies the printed text faithfully, so this is not a transcription difference.
